new_written_lead_not_promoted.statement: Let P_A be the primes of |A| and M_Z the product of the prime-power parts of n over primes NOT dividing |A|. If M_Z >= 14 (equivalently M_Z divides none of 1..13), then a minimal B/D2 trade of size EXACTLY 7 forces A mod (n/M_Z) to be PERIODIC.
new_written_lead_not_promoted.proof: Lemma F' (multiplier d=1 mod n/M_Z, d=0 mod M_Z, prime to |A|) makes every M_Z-fibre of B and of D2 a complement of A_N, N=n/M_Z, of size N/|A|. Fibrewise the trade gives A_N+N_y = A_N+P_y with |P_y|=|N_y|. The seven trade seeds 2,4,6 (P) and 1,7,13,14 (N) have pairwise differences 1..13, so they lie in seven distinct fibres. Each N-seed fibre needs a P-element and each P-seed fibre an N-element; the 4+3 unknown elements of a size-7 trade are thus used one per fibre. Every affected fibre has |P_y|=|N_y|=1, so p_y - n_y (nonzero, the elements share the M_Z-coordinate) is a period of A_N.

Applies only when M_Z >= 14; if every prime of n divides |A| the fibration is trivial.
